evals.prompt: need a dialog and a button in my dioxus 0.7 app, want the official ones not some random lib. what do i run and what do i have to wire up after
evals.expected_output: dx --version check, the Dioxus.toml registry check, the complete `dx components add dialog button --git https://github.com/DioxusLabs/dioxus-components --rev <40-hex>` command shown for approval (not run), a mandatory diff of the copied files against the repository at that SHA, then mod components;, the theme stylesheet, a pinned dioxus-primitives git dependency, and a Cargo.lock commit.
expectations: The answer gives `dx components add` with the component names (`dialog`, `button`) as the install method.

The command shown includes both `--git https://github.com/DioxusLabs/dioxus-components` and `--rev` with a full 40-hex commit SHA (or a clearly marked placeholder for one), and the answer says the SHA must be one the user has reviewed.
The answer says `--rev` is ignored when `--git` is not given.
The answer says the default registry is unpinned (it tracks the latest `main`).
[transcript-only] The agent shows the complete command to the user for approval and does not run `dx components add` itself.
The answer says to check `Dioxus.toml` for a `[components.registry]` override before adding.
The answer says to compare the copied component files, the theme asset and the `Cargo.toml` changes with the repository at the chosen SHA after the add.
The answer tells the user to confirm `mod components;` is in `main.rs` and to link `dx-components-theme.css` once with `document::Stylesheet` and `asset!`, regardless of what the CLI printed.
The answer says to pin the `dioxus-primitives` git dependency in `Cargo.toml` with the same `rev` and to commit `Cargo.lock`.
The answer does not suggest `cargo add dioxus-primitives` or `cargo add dioxus-components`.

evals.prompt: i tried cargo add dioxus-primitives and it gave me 0.0.0 and nothing in it works. then i found dioxus-components on crates.io 0.1.2 - is that the official one? which do i use
evals.expected_output: Explains that crates.io dioxus-primitives is a placeholder (0.0.0), that crates.io dioxus-components is an unrelated third-party crate, and gives the git dependency with a rev (or dx components add) as the supported route.
expectations: The answer states that `dioxus-primitives` on crates.io is a `0.0.0` placeholder rather than the real library.
The answer states that `dioxus-components` on crates.io is not the official DioxusLabs registry (it is an unrelated third-party crate).
The answer recommends a git dependency on `https://github.com/DioxusLabs/dioxus-components` with a pinned `rev`, or `dx components add`, as the way to get the primitives.
The answer does not recommend using either crates.io crate.
The answer does not claim that every crates.io dependency in registry manifests is unsafe (crates such as `time` are ordinary dependencies).

evals.prompt: the installed button is white-on-white in dark mode on some pages and i want a brand blue primary + a manual dark mode toggle. theme file has these weird var(--dark, #000) var(--light, #fff) values, how do i override without breaking it
evals.expected_output: Use html[data-theme] to force a scheme; override variables in a stylesheet loaded after the theme file using the same two-branch form, or style via data attributes; do not edit the vendored theme; check contrast in both schemes.
expectations: The answer sets the colour scheme by putting `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on the `html` element.
The answer puts overrides in a separate stylesheet that is loaded after `dx-components-theme.css` instead of editing the theme file.
Any re-declared colour variable uses the same `var(--dark, ...) var(--light, ...)` two-branch form as the theme file.
The component-specific override selector targets `data-style` / `data-size` attributes (for example `[data-style="primary"]`) and not the hashed CSS-module class name.
The answer tells the user to check text contrast in both light and dark schemes after changing variables.
The answer warns that `dx components add --force` overwrites local edits to copied component files.
The answer says hover, focus and disabled states have their own, more specific rules in the component stylesheet, so each state that is restyled needs its own override.
The component-specific override selector includes the element name (for example `button[data-style="primary"]`) so that it outranks the component's own `.dx-button[data-style="primary"]` rule.

evals.expected_output: Tabs and Dialog have same-name entries; toasts map to `toast` as the nearest entry; Table, Carousel, Drawer have no registry entry (Sheet is the nearest side panel) and no invented install commands.
expectations: The answer maps Tabs to `tabs` and Dialog to `dialog`.
The answer maps toast notifications to `toast` and notes Sonner itself is a different library, so the match is approximate.
The answer states that Table and Carousel have no entry in the dioxus-components registry.
The answer does not give a `dx components add table` or `dx components add carousel` command as if those components existed.
The answer says Drawer has no registry entry and may mention `sheet` as the nearest side-panel component.
The answer says that a same-name match means the names correspond and that behaviour should still be checked, or tells the user to confirm names with `dx components list`.

evals.prompt: added a dialog with an X icon button to close it. a coworker says its not accessible. keyboard users get lost. what should i check
evals.expected_output: Checks: accessible name on the icon-only button, dialog title via aria_labelledby, primitives already trap focus/Escape, visible focus indicator, contrast, focus return, keyboard-only pass.
expectations: The answer says the icon-only close button needs an accessible name such as `aria_label`.

The answer says the dialog needs a `DialogTitle` (and optionally a `DialogDescription`), which are wired to `aria_labelledby` / `aria_describedby` through the dialog context, so the ids should not be wired by hand.
The answer says the dialog primitive traps focus when modal and closes on Escape on web and webview renderers, so those should not be hand-rolled.
The answer says a visible `:focus-visible` indicator must be preserved when overriding styles.
The answer includes a keyboard-only test (Tab order, Enter/Space activation, Escape) as part of the check.

evals.expected_output: Registry components are plain CSS modules and do not need Tailwind; if both are used, link theme, then the Tailwind output, then overrides [unverified: the cascade should be checked in the browser].
expectations: The answer states that the registry components do not require Tailwind (they ship plain CSS module stylesheets).
The answer does not claim that Tailwind must be added in order to style the registry components.

evals.prompt: i pinned dioxus-primitives in Cargo.toml to a sha, then ran dx components add date_picker --rev <same sha> and date_picker, calendar and popover all look newer than that sha and the build fails. what happened
evals.expected_output: Explains that --rev is ignored without --git (dx 0.7.10 source), so everything came from the default registry's latest main; the corrected command adds --git; with --git and --rev, adding date_picker directly is expected to abort with a Cannot copy global asset error because built-in dependencies resolve from the default registry (DioxusLabs/dioxus#5310); the primary approach is to add the dependency components first, each as a separate earlier command, then compare with the SHA.
expectations: The answer says `--rev` is ignored when `--git` is not given (in the dx 0.7.10 source), so all the components came from the default registry's latest `main`.
The corrected command in the answer includes `--git https://github.com/DioxusLabs/dioxus-components` together with the full `--rev`.

The answer says that with `--git` and `--rev`, adding `date_picker` directly is expected to abort with a `Cannot copy global asset ... outside of the component registry` error, because its built-in dependencies (`calendar`, `popover`) resolve from the default registry (DioxusLabs/dioxus#5310), and labels this as source-derived rather than run.
The answer proposes adding the dependency components (`calendar`, `popover`) first, each as a separate earlier command with the same `--git` and `--rev`, as the primary approach.
The answer tells the user to compare the copied files, the theme asset and the `Cargo.toml` changes with the repository at the chosen SHA.
The answer says the pin should be a full 40-hex SHA.

evals.prompt: i ran dx components add color_picker --git https://github.com/DioxusLabs/dioxus-components --rev <the sha i reviewed> and it died with: Error: Cannot copy global asset '<cache>/preview/assets/dx-components-theme.css' for component 'popover' because it is outside of the component registry '<other cache>'. now Cargo.toml changed and there's a src/components/popover folder. what do i do
evals.expected_output: Identifies the known gap DioxusLabs/dioxus#5310 (built-in dependency resolved from the default registry cache outside the pinned registry root); notes cargo add already ran and partial copies may exist; gives cleanup (review git diff, revert Cargo.toml changes, remove partial directories, re-run fails with Destination directory already exists unless removed); then dependency components first as separate commands, labelled untested, then compare with the SHA.
expectations: The answer identifies the error as the known upstream gap DioxusLabs/dioxus#5310: a built-in dependency (`popover`) was resolved from the default registry's cache, outside the pinned registry's root.
The answer says `cargo add` had already modified `Cargo.toml` before the abort, so the user should review and revert unwanted changes (for example with `git diff`).

The answer says a partially copied component directory (here `popover`) may exist that is not registered in `mod.rs`, and tells the user to delete it or remove it with `dx components remove` before retrying.
The answer says a re-run fails with `Destination directory ... already exists` for a requested component that survived the cleanup, and that only `--force` overwrites.
The answer recommends adding the dependency components (`popover`, `input`) first, each as a separate command with the same `--git` and `--rev`, and labels this approach as untested or unverified.
The answer tells the user to compare the copied files, the theme asset and the `Cargo.toml` changes with the repository at the chosen SHA.
[transcript-only] The agent does not run `dx components` commands itself.
